title: Asking about a trip

Asking about a trip

Stage 4 · Recall

Recall

2The film was three hours of nothing. It was so ___.

got lost · boring · stayed · awful · lucky · went sightseeing.

Stage 5 · Grammar

Grammar

didn't and Did you…?
Track 8.7 — three fast questionsOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
How long did you stay? · Did you like the food? · Did he stay in hotels?
1Question 1 was…
2Question 2 was…
3Question 3 was…
Why

/dɪdʒə/ = did you · /dɪdi/ = did he. Fast speech hides the words — but the meaning is the same.

1Question 1 was…
2Question 3 was…
Why

/dɪdʒə/ = did you · /dɪdi/ = did he.

1Question 1 was…
2Question 3 was…
Why

/dɪdʒə/ = did you · /dɪdi/ = did he.

In other words
“Did you go on your own?” — “Yes, I did.”
“Where did you go?”
“How long did you stay?”
“I didn't stay in hotels.”
Notice

Notice: after did and didn't — is the verb went / stayed, or go / stay?

FormExample
NegativeI didn't stay in hotels.
QuestionDid you go on your own?
Wh- questionWhere did you go? · How long did you stay?
Short answerYes, I did. / No, I didn't.
In other words
Negative: didn't + base verb — I didn't like the food (NOT didn't liked).
Question: Did + person + base verb — Did you go? (NOT Did you went).
The past lives in did — so the main verb goes back to its base form.
Short answers: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
This works for ALL verbs — regular and irregular.

Stage 6 · Practice

Practice

Part 1 — Choose the correct verb form.
Track 7.7 — four things that didn't happenOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
Fauja didn't run marathons when he was young. He didn't have a lot of problems when he lived on his family's farm. His happy life didn't continue after he had a family. He didn't stop after his first marathon.
1Did you ___ to the beach?
2Where did she ___?
3Did they ___ the museum?
4I didn't ___ the food.
5We didn't ___ a good time.
6Did he ___ lost?
Why

After did / didn't → base verb: go, stay, visit, like, have, get.

1❌ “Did you went to Spain?”
2❌ “She didn't took photos.”
3❌ “Where you did stay?”
4❌ “Yes, I didn't.”
Why

Did you go · didn't take · Where did you stay? · No, I didn't (yes goes with did).

1Fauja ___ marathons when he was young.
2His happy life ___ after he had a family.
3He ___ after his first marathon.
Why

didn't + base: didn't run, didn't continue, didn't stop. The irregular pasts (ran, had, lived) stay in positive sentences.

1Did you ___ a good time?
2Why did they ___ home early?
3She didn't ___ the museum.
4We didn't ___ lost — we had a map!
Why

After did / didn't → base verb: have, leave, visit, get.

1❌ “Did she went to the beach?”
2❌ “We didn't saw the ruins.”
3❌ “What did you ate?”
Why

Did she go · didn't see · What did you eat? The past lives in did.

1Fauja ___ marathons when he was young.
2He ___ after his first marathon.
Why

didn't + base: didn't run, didn't stop.

1Did you ___ a good time?
2Why did they ___ home early?
3She didn't ___ the museum.
4We didn't ___ lost — we had a map!
Why

After did / didn't → base verb: have, leave, visit, get.

1❌ “Did she went to the beach?”
2❌ “We didn't saw the ruins.”
3❌ “What did you ate?”
Why

Did she go · didn't see · What did you eat? The past lives in did.

1Fauja ___ marathons when he was young.
2He ___ after his first marathon.
Why

didn't + base: didn't run, didn't stop.

Stage 7 · Listen

Listen

Track 8.3 — the Guatemala interviewOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
K: So you went to Guatemala on holiday this time? Where is it exactly? T: It's in Central America, to the south of Mexico. K: Why did you go there? T: Because it's a really interesting country. I wanted to go sightseeing and see some of the famous ruined Mayan cities and temples. K: And whereabouts in Guatemala did you go? T: I visited the whole country. I started in Antigua — the historic capital — and then I went to Lake Atitlán, a beautiful lake in the mountains. K: So what did you do and see? T: I went on lots of tours, and I went trekking in the rainforest. My favourite thing was the ruins of a Mayan city in Tikal. I climbed to the top of a temple at sunrise. K: Wow! It sounds fantastic. T: It was. I took a lot of pictures! K: And how long did you stay? T: About six weeks. K: Did you stay in hotels? T: No, mostly guest houses, and I also stayed with a Guatemalan family. They were lovely and it really helped me with my Spanish. K: Did you go on your own? T: Yes, I did, but I met lots of local people and I made lots of new friends.
Tom is back from a trip. A friend asks him about it.

Listen once for the big picture. Then listen again for the details.

1Where did Tom go?
Why

Guatemala — in Central America, to the south of Mexico.

1Why did he go there?
2What was his favourite thing?
3How long did he stay?
4Did he stay in hotels?
5Did he go on his own?
Why

An interesting country · the ruins in Tikal · six weeks · mostly guest houses + a family · yes, alone — but he made lots of friends.

1“___ did you go there?” — “Because it's interesting.”
2“___ did you stay?” — “About six weeks.”
3“___ did you do and see?” — “Lots of tours.”
Why

Why → because… · How long → six weeks · What → lots of tours.

Stage 8 · Write

Write

Track 8.5 — the question bankOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
1 Where did you go on your last holiday? 2 Did you go with a friend? 3 What did you do? 4 Did you have a good time? 5 How long did you stay? 6 Where did you stay? 7 Did you like the food?
Listen to the seven questions. Then answer them in writing — about YOUR last trip.

Full sentences. Use didn't at least once.

Useful language

  • I stayed in…
  • I visited…
  • I didn't…
  • It was interesting / awful
  • I was lucky —…

Stage 9 · Type it

Type it

Now produce it — type, don’t tap.

Spelling counts. Type the answers, then check.

1I ___ go out last night. (negative)
2___ you see the film?
3Did you ___ to the beach? (go)
Why

didn't + base verb (didn't go, not didn't went) \u00b7 Did you + base verb? \u00b7 short answer: Yes, I did.

1I didn't went out.
2Did you saw the film?
3She didn't was happy.
Why

didn't + base verb (didn't go, not didn't went) \u00b7 Did you + base verb? \u00b7 short answer: Yes, I did.

1Make it negative: We had a good time.
2Make a question: You went to the beach.
3Answer with YES: Did you like it?
Why

didn't + base verb (didn't go, not didn't went) \u00b7 Did you + base verb? \u00b7 short answer: Yes, I did.
